# Appendix B: The datasets {.unnumbered}

*Every market the book measures on, where its days come from, and the units its numbers are in. Each one reaches the
tools through a format plug-in (chapter 14) as days of ticks, so every tool can be pointed at any of them.*

## Prosperity 2, 3 and 4: the stand-in

IMC Prosperity is a yearly online trading competition, each round with a few days of data, and that data is what the whole
prep ran on in place of the Arena's. A day is 10,000 ticks, at timestamps 0 to 999,900 in steps of 100, for 54 of the
69 days here; the other 15, tutorial and submission data, are 2,000 or 1,000 ticks long. Each tick
has three book levels a side and the trades printed since the last one; prices and PnL are in **credits**. A product's
book is generated by IMC's simulator: a large quote at about the value, the "wall", that chapter 3 builds the fair
value on, and takers who mostly don't know more than it.

The days come with three open-source backtesters, cloned into the references folder at pinned commits: jmerle's for
Prosperity 2 and 3 and another author's for Prosperity 4. The data names p2, p3 and p4 point at their data folders
[(`references/clone.sh`; `python/arena/formats/prosperity.py`, `DATA_DIRS`)]{.src}. Between them they hold 69 days
[(`data/datasets.csv`, from `prosperity.list_days`; the tick counts from `prosperity.load_days`)]{.src}:

| Data | Rounds | Days | Products, for example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `p2` | 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 | 20 | Amethysts and Starfruit; a gift basket and its three legs; Coconut and its coupon |
| `p3` | 0 to 8 | 32 | Rainforest Resin, Kelp and Squid Ink; two picnic baskets and their legs; Volcanic Rock and five vouchers; Magnificent Macarons |
| `p4` | 0 to 5 | 17 | Osmium and Pepper Root; Hydrogel, Velvetfruit and ten vouchers; 50 products in round 5 |

::: {.content-visible when-format="audio"}
Prosperity 2 has 20 days in six rounds, with Amethysts and Starfruit, a gift basket and its legs, and an option on
Coconut. Prosperity 3 has 32 days in nine rounds, from Kelp and Resin to baskets, vouchers and Macarons. Prosperity 4
has 17 days in six rounds, ending with a round of 50 products.
:::

Two cautions. Prosperity 2 has no round 2 here: its conversions aren't supported, by its backtester or by ours. And
the higher-numbered rounds are not new markets: in Prosperity 3, round 6 holds the data the submissions ran on, round 7
the end-of-round data and round 8 an earlier version of round 2, and Prosperity reuses days across rounds, so a day can
be "unseen" in name only. `arena.grid` flags days that share their books and trades (`repeated_days`)
[(`references/prosperity3-backtester-jmerle/README.md:79-81`; `ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Grid search")]{.src}. Some rounds
name the traders behind each trade, which the copy mode of chapter 8 uses: Prosperity 2's rounds 1, 3 and 4,
Prosperity 3's round 5 and day 5 of its round 6, and Prosperity 4's round 4.

Our engine reproduces the Prosperity 3 backtester fill for fill in its default mode, so a result here is the result
that backtester would give (chapter 14). It is still a result about IMC's generator.

## `arena.sim`: a market that reacts

A replay can't react to our orders; `arena.sim` can. It is our own agent-based market [(`python/arena/sim.py`)]{.src}: each
tick a fundamental price moves, a market maker re-quotes its walls, limit traders post near the value, the book is
shown to the bots, and then noise, value and momentum takers trade against it, the bots' orders included. Every seed is
a new day, and a run with a bot and the recording without it share every random number, so the gap between them is the
market's reaction [(`README.md`, "Simulated market")]{.src}.

Its presets copy products the prep knew: `KELP`, `RAINFOREST_RESIN` and `SQUID_INK`, calibrated so that
`arena.diagnose` reads them as Prosperity 3's round 1, are the default market; `HYDROGEL_PACK`, `KELP_FLOW`,
`KELP_NOISY`, `ROBOT_DISHES` and `LARGE_TICK` add a level, one-sided takers, a maker that doesn't know the price, jumps
and a one-tick book. `generate` writes days in Prosperity's layout, prices in credits; `run` puts a bot inside the
market and compares it with replaying the same days. `--regime` shifts or trends every price from mid-day.

It is a market we wrote, calibrated to the one we already had, so it tests how a bot meets a reaction, not whether
Prosperity's premise holds.

## ABIDES: a market we didn't write

ABIDES is JP Morgan's public agent-based market simulator, cloned with the other references
[(`references/abides-jpmc`)]{.src}. Its RMSC04
configuration is one stock, `ABM`, traded from 09:30 to 16:00 by 1,000 noise agents, 102 value agents who see a noisy
view of a hidden mean-reverting value, 12 momentum agents and 2 adaptive market makers. Its book has no wall at the
value, and its value agents carry information: it is the "market unlike Prosperity" the prep needed
[(`python/experiments/abides_days.py`)]{.src}.

`experiments.abides_days` runs it in its own environment and converts each day to Prosperity's layout: a tick a second,
23,400 a day, three levels a side, prices in **cents**, a limit of 100, and the trades of the second after each
snapshot, without names. A file beside each day holds the hidden value, the answer key no real market gives. The
book's ABIDES numbers come from 10 days, seeds 1 to 10, kept out of git, since the seeds make them again
[(`data/abides/`; `IDEAS.md`, "An independent generator: ABIDES's RMSC04")]{.src}. It is a recording too: it tests the book and the
agents' information, not a market that reacts to us.

## LOBSTER: a real book, still to come

LOBSTER sells reconstructed NASDAQ order books, message by message; its sample days would give the prep a real market's
informed flow beside ABIDES's simulated one. The converter is written (`experiments.lobster_days`, the same layout as
ABIDES's, prices in cents), but the files are not: the samples are no longer a public download, so a person has to
request them [(`TODO.md`, "LOBSTER's sample, one stock at level 5"; `docs/MANUAL_TODO.md`, "LOBSTER's sample files")]{.src}.
Nothing in this book is measured on LOBSTER.

## The mock rounds: rehearsals in disguise

Four rehearsals of the day, each made by an agent out of sight of the sessions that played it, in
`python/experiments/mock_round/`. Each takes `arena.sim` products, renames and reprices them, and writes them in a
layout and bot interface unlike any in the repo, with public days to work on, hidden days that score, and a portal.
Each is in its own units:

| Rehearsal | Date | What it tested | Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meridian (`mock_round/`) | 26 October | the kickoff prompts, with and without the repo | credits |
| Halden Exchange (`round2/`) | 28 October | the repo before and after its restructure | credits; prices in pips of 0.25 credits |
| Kestrel Bourse (`round3/`) | 30 October | unstated rules: strict fills, last-trade mark, orders a step late | credits; prices in points worth 2 credits |
| Varde Exchange (`round4/`) | 3 November | a portal that is not our engine | euros; prices in cents |

::: {.content-visible when-format="audio"}
Four mock rounds: Meridian on 26 October, which tested the kickoff prompts; the Halden Exchange on 28 October, the repo
before and after its restructure; the Kestrel Bourse on 30 October, rules left unstated, among them orders arriving a
step late; and the Varde Exchange on 3 November, whose portal is not our engine. The first three score in credits, the
Varde in euros.
:::

All four are spent: their answer keys are committed, so a new rehearsal needs a new round
[(`python/experiments/mock_round/README.md`, `round2/README.md`, `round3/README.md`, `round4/README.md`, each "Spent")]{.src}.
Their results are in the ideas file's row "The kickoff prompts on a disguised round". The drill format has practice data of its own, three simulated days that `experiments.format_drill`
writes in it.

## The Arena

The Arena's own data arrives with each round, into a folder of its own. It stays out of git, except each round's
handover note and saved leaderboard, which are the record appendix E is written from
[(`data/arena/round<N>/`, `HANDOVER.md`, `leaderboard.json`)]{.src}. Until the event the folder is
empty, and nothing in this book is measured on it.

## The zoo is bots, not data

The zoo folder of bots is easy to mistake for a dataset, and it isn't one. It holds 32 bots written by language
models, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and local models, each given only a Prosperity-style spec and one of four prompts: a
baseline, a market maker, mean reversion and momentum [(`python/bots/zoo/`, `SPEC.md`, `PROMPTS.md`)]{.src}. They are
what a team that hands the rules to a model would start from, so they are the baseline the template must beat and a
population of rivals to trade against in one market. They
run on any of the data above like any other bot; they are never edited once written, and each has a Rust twin
[(`python/bots/zoo/README.md`)]{.src}.
